sections.h2: Where is Spring Valley, and how does its layout affect a sale?
sections.html:
Spring Valley is a dense village in Rockland County, about 22 miles north of Manhattan and 5 miles north of the New Jersey line. Most of it lies in the Town of Ramapo, with a small western slice in the Town of Clarkstown. Neighbors include Chestnut Ridge to the south, Airmont and Monsey to the west, Hillcrest to the north and Nanuet to the east.

The village is next to the New York State Thruway (Interstate 87), and the Spring Valley Transit Center is the terminus of New Jersey Transit's Pascack Valley Line. That access to rail and highway is a selling point for commuters. The village began as a railroad stop: the New York and Erie Railroad called the area Pascack in 1842, and residents chose Spring Valley after a large spring in Valley Pond. Downtown revitalization has meant demolishing abandoned buildings on Main Street and putting mixed-use buildings in their place.

Because the village straddles two towns, the town part of your tax bill depends on the side of the line your parcel is on. Your deed, tax bill and the county's property search will show it.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about housing in Spring Valley?
sections.html:
Spring Valley is crowded and rent-heavy. The Census Bureau counts 2.01 square miles of land and 16,442.6 residents per square mile, with 34,482 people estimated for July 1, 2025, up 4.3% from the 2020 base. Only 25.0% of homes are owner-occupied, and households average 3.63 people.

The population is young and multilingual: 36.0% of residents are under 18, 8.9% are 65 or older, and 75.6% of residents age five and up speak a language other than English at home. Marketing materials in more than one language may reach more of the buyers and tenants in the village.

With three-quarters of homes rented, a lot of Spring Valley sellers own two-family and multi-family buildings with tenants in place. If yours is one of them, gather leases, rent rolls and any inspection records before you talk to buyers.

sections.h2: Which village office handles permits and certificates of occupancy?
sections.html:
The Village of Spring Valley Building Department, at 200 North Main Street, administers the New York State Building Code, Fire Prevention Code, Housing Code and Energy Code along with the village's planning and zoning rules. It issues building permits, certificates of occupancy and water meters, schedules construction inspections and takes complaints. Its inspectors also carry out fire code and housing inspections.

That mix of housing inspections and certificate work makes the department the first call if your house has an unfinished project, an extra apartment or an open complaint. Village Hall answers at (845) 352-1100. The village website links to the Rockland County property search and an interactive county map, which help you confirm lot lines and the correct town.

  • Ask whether every unit in your building has a certificate of occupancy.
  • Ask whether any housing or fire inspection is open.
  • Ask whether the village requires any registration or certificate when a house with tenants changes owners.

sections.h2: How are Spring Valley property taxes billed?
sections.html:
A Spring Valley owner usually receives three kinds of tax bill, and they come from different offices. Village taxes are billed and collected by the village itself, and the Town of Ramapo states plainly that it does not collect taxes for the villages. The Village Treasurer's Office at Village Hall takes payments and posts due dates on the bill and in the village's tax portal.

Ramapo's Receiver of Taxes collects the County and Town bill, with the first payment due on or before January 31 and penalties starting in February. School tax penalties start in October. Taxpayers with a bill over $50 may pay the County and Town tax in four installments, with a 5% service charge collected by the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance. School taxes arrive on a separate bill.

Ramapo's tax office gives sellers direct advice: do not use the installment plan when you plan to sell, because it can cause confusion at closing and the service fee is 5% of the total. At closing you receive credit for the unused portion of the taxes. Under state law an owner stays responsible for taxes even if a bill never arrives, and the town cannot waive statutory penalties.

sections.h2: How is a Spring Valley deed recorded in Rockland County?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded by the Rockland County Clerk at 1 South Main Street in New City. The clerk does not supply deed forms and cannot help prepare one. The deed has to be signed and notarized, include the names and addresses of all sellers and buyers, and carry a Schedule A property description, which you can copy from the current deed of record.

  • Form TP-584 must be signed by all parties, and Form RP-5217 needs at least one grantor and one grantee, with a buyer contact name and a valid phone number.
  • The base recording fee is $45, plus $5 per page, a $6 TP-584 fee and a $10 notification fee.
  • The RP-5217 filing fee is $125 or $250, depending on the property class code and the sale type on the form.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope must come with a mailed submission, or the recorded original is not returned.

The transfer tax listed by the clerk is $2 per $500, or $4 per $1,000. On $381,800, the typical owner-occupied value in the village, that comes to $1,528. The 1% mansion tax applies only when the taxable consideration is $1 million or more.

sections.h2: What should a Spring Valley seller line up before contract?
sections.html:
Start with the parcel: confirm the town, the school district and the village tax account from your bills. Then collect permit records and certificates of occupancy from the Building Department, and ask for the tax status of the village, County and Town, and school bills. A closing attorney can then prepare the deed, Schedule A and transfer forms.

Ramapo's tax office handles school and property taxes for about 30,000 parcels, keeps the tax roll open for public inspection, and says it assists residents, realtors, lenders and title companies who need tax information. A Third Party Request Form is listed on its page.

If the building has tenants, add leases, rent ledgers and any inspection notices to the file. Buyers of multi-family buildings in a village where only a quarter of homes are owner-occupied will want to know exactly who lives in each unit and what each pays.

faqs.q: Does the Town of Ramapo collect my Spring Valley village taxes?
faqs.a: No. Ramapo states that each village bills and collects its own taxes. In Spring Valley that means the Village Treasurer's Office at 200 North Main Street.

faqs.q: Should I choose installments if I plan to sell in Spring Valley?
faqs.a: No. Ramapo's Receiver of Taxes advises against it because of closing confusion and the 5% service fee. At closing you are credited for the unused part of the taxes.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Spring Valley deed?
faqs.a: The Rockland County Clerk in New City records it. The deed must be signed and notarized, and Forms TP-584 and RP-5217 go with it.

faqs.q: What does recording a deed cost in Rockland County?
faqs.a: The clerk lists a $45 base fee, $5 per page, a $6 TP-584 fee and a $10 notification fee, plus transfer tax and the RP-5217 fee of $125 or $250.

faqs.q: Who inspects houses and issues certificates of occupancy in Spring Valley?
faqs.a: The village Building Department at 200 North Main Street. It enforces the state building, fire, housing and energy codes and handles permits and certificates.
